title: Human State Interface (HSI) 1.4
$comment: HSI 1.4 canonical schema (RFC-HSI-0012). Builds on 1.3 by adding a required per-reading `status` (estimated / stated / insufficient_evidence / withheld), a lean abstention shape (name, status, reason, window_ids) for readings without a value, `basis` and `baseline_version` saying what a score is relative to, and `valid_until` from the producer. Also adds an optional `meta.context` frame per window with closed per-field vocabularies, including environment fields. A reading with no estimate has a legal shape, so producers no longer omit configured members (RFC-HSI-0012 §5.6). `confidence` MAY be null only on `external_provider` readings. `confidence_breakdown` is deprecated and scheduled for removal in 1.5 (RFC-HSI-0011 §9). Everything else is carried over from 1.3 unchanged. Some reference-integrity constraints MUST be enforced out-of-band for HSI-VALIDATE-STRICT compliance.

observed_at_utc.$comment: Event-time: the human state time (typically aligns with the latest window end).

computed_at_utc.$comment: Processing-time: when this payload was produced. Must be >= observed_at_utc (enforced out-of-band unless validator supports format comparisons).

windows.$comment: Map keys are the authoritative window IDs. axis_reading.window_ids and embedding.window_ids SHOULD reference these keys.

hsi_id.$comment: Unique identifier for this HSI payload instance (RFC 4122 UUID). Used for deduplication, logging, and cross-system correlation.

ids.$comment: Stable document-level identifiers. `hsi_id` is required; producers MAY add other id keys (e.g. subject_id, session_id) under `ids`.

context.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §7. Map from window id to the conditions under which that window's readings were made. Keys MUST be keys of /windows (HSI-1.4-CONTEXT-UNKNOWN-WINDOW). Emitted only when the consumer is permitted to receive context; there is no withheld form, so an unpermitted frame is omitted.

meta.$comment: Required since 1.3. `meta.ids.hsi_id` MUST be a UUID. `meta.provenance` is the canonical place for source tracking. `meta.context` (1.4) carries the per-window context frame. Additional producer-defined keys are permitted.

source_tier.$comment: Architectural signal-fidelity tier declared on a source in meta.provenance.sources. 1 = ground-truth (RR intervals, raw sensor stream, lab-grade ECG), 2 = vendor-derived high-fidelity, 3 = proxy time-series (≤1 Hz HR traces, motion-derived proxies), 4 = snapshot/minimal. Higher tier numbers SHOULD correspond to reduced downstream trust. Distinct from `source.quality` (transient/situational reliability in `[0, 1]`); a source can have `source_tier: 1, quality: 0.3` (architecturally ground-truth, currently degraded) or `source_tier: 3, quality: 0.95` (architecturally proxy-only, currently clean signal). The tier table is physiology-flavored; for non-physio sources producers SHOULD pick the closest analog along the raw → aggregate spectrum (raw events ≈ Tier 1, aggregated rollup ≈ Tier 4). Readings and embeddings derive an effective tier consumer-side by resolving evidence_source_ids and taking the most conservative (highest-numbered) tier among cited sources. See RFC-HSI-0008 §6.7.

observable_modality.$comment: RFC-HSI-0010 §6 observable modality set. The fourth canonical modality `multimodal` is a fusion outcome and is NOT a valid observable; it cannot appear in modalities_used or as a confidence_breakdown key.

window.$comment: HSI-VALIDATE-STRICT: window.end_utc MUST be >= window.start_utc (out-of-band unless validator supports format comparisons).

direction.$comment: RFC-HSI-0010 §7. `lower_is_more` replaces 1.2's `higher_is_less` (semantic clarification, not behavioral). `categorical` (new in 1.3) marks readings that carry a discrete class label rather than a scalar score; gated by §8.

inference_mode.$comment: probabilistic_model: learned/ensemble. deterministic_rule: formulas/rulepacks. external_provider: third-party or OS facts. composite: merged multi-source. Orthogonal to modality (encoded by axis-domain key, RFC-HSI-0010 §5.3).

status.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §5.1. estimated: computed from evidence in its windows. stated: the person's own value for this member and window. insufficient_evidence: configured and attempted, but no estimate this window. withheld: estimable, but the consumer is not permitted to receive it. Freshness is not a status: a republished estimate stays estimated and its valid_until says whether it is still current (§5.4).

reason.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §5.2. Required when status is insufficient_evidence or withheld; forbidden when status is estimated or stated. not_granted is the only reason for withheld. RFC-HSI-0010 §9 `modality_unavailable` corresponds to `no_signal`.

basis.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §5.3. What a normalized score is relative to. Absent means unspecified and MUST NOT be read as personal. meta.provenance.baseline_status is informative only and MUST NOT be used in place of basis to gate a reading.

resolution.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §5.4.2. Set when score is reported coarser than the producer's estimate: the estimate lies in [lower, upper] and score is the value reported for that band. Absent means score is the estimate at full resolution. HSI-VALIDATE-STRICT checks lower < upper and lower <= score <= upper.

axis_reading.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §5.1. Two shapes, selected by status. Value-bearing (estimated, stated): the full 1.3 reading plus status. Abstention (insufficient_evidence, withheld): name, status, reason, window_ids, and nothing that looks like a value.

name.$comment: Axis member name. RFC-HSI-0010 §4.1–§4.5 list canonical members per domain; SHOULD be lowercase-snake-case but the schema does not enforce a pattern (1.2 compat). Unknown names within a known domain MUST be tolerated (RFC-HSI-0008 §6.5).

score.$comment: Required on estimated and stated readings; null there only when direction == categorical (label carries the value). Absent on abstentions: a missing estimate is expressed by status, never by a null score.

confidence.$comment: Required on estimated and stated readings. RFC-HSI-0012 §5.4.1: null only when inference_mode == external_provider, for relayed provider scores that carry no uncertainty. Absent on abstentions.

model_id.$comment: URI-shaped identifier (RFC 3986 scheme + path). Reserved schemes: 'model://', 'rulepack://', 'provider://', and 'stated://' (1.4; RECOMMENDED for person-stated readings, not enforced: status is the single signal that a reading is stated). Optional on insufficient_evidence readings (the model that abstained).

reason_detail.$comment: Optional producer-defined finer cause (e.g. `device_off_body`) on insufficient_evidence readings. Not part of the contract: consumers MUST NOT branch on its values.

baseline_version.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §5.3.1: opaque identifier of the version of the reference the score is relative to. Two readings with the same basis are comparable only when their baseline_version also matches. Requires basis.

valid_until.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §5.4. Latest instant at which the producer stands behind the value. Consumers MUST NOT act on a reading whose valid_until has passed. A republished estimate keeps its original valid_until, so an expired value is self-evident. Value-bearing readings only.

items.$comment: entries SHOULD reference keys in meta.provenance.sources. Channel-fidelity information lives on each source descriptor (`quality`, `signals`, `degraded`).

evidence_source_ids.$comment: Required on value-bearing readings. Optional on insufficient_evidence readings, where it lists the sources that were tried. Forbidden on withheld readings.

modalities_used.$comment: RFC-HSI-0010 §5.1 as relaxed by RFC-HSI-0012 §6.5. Required on estimated readings in axes.cognitive[] and axes.affective[]; optional on stated readings there; forbidden on abstentions and on readings in axes.physiological[] / axes.kinematic[] / axes.digital[].

confidence_breakdown.$comment: DEPRECATED in 1.4, scheduled for removal in 1.5 (RFC-HSI-0012 §9 applying the RFC-HSI-0011 §9 rule: no canonical producer populates it consistently and no canonical consumer reads it). Still accepted so existing producers keep validating. Per-channel confidence attribution on multimodal readings only; rejected on single-modality readings via axes_domain_single_modality. Keys SHOULD be a subset of modalities_used (HSI-VALIDATE-STRICT).

label.$comment: Categorical class label. Required when direction == categorical, forbidden otherwise. MUST appear in `categories` (HSI-VALIDATE-STRICT).

categories.$comment: Full set of possible categories the producer may emit for this axis member. Required when direction == categorical, forbidden otherwise.

allOf.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §6.3 rule 1: estimates and statements carry the full value shape and no reason.
RFC-HSI-0012 §6.3 rule 2: an abstention says why and carries nothing that could be read as a value.
RFC-HSI-0012 §5.1.1 and §6.3 rule 3: withheld discloses that the member exists and nothing more.

RFC-HSI-0010 §8: discriminated union on direction == categorical. Abstentions have no direction, so this applies to value-bearing readings only. A categorical label is already coarse, so it carries no resolution (RFC-HSI-0012 §5.4.2).
RFC-HSI-0012 §5.4.1: confidence may be null only on relayed provider readings.
RFC-HSI-0012 §5.3.1: a baseline version only makes sense alongside the basis it versions.
RFC-HSI-0010 §5.1 + RFC-HSI-0011 §4.2: modalities_used and confidence_breakdown are forbidden on readings in single-modality domains; the axis-domain key already encodes the modality.
RFC-HSI-0010 §5.1 as relaxed by RFC-HSI-0012 §6.5: modalities_used is required on estimated readings only. confidence_breakdown is permitted but optional and deprecated.

axes.$comment: RFC-HSI-0010 §4: closed 5-domain set. Adding a domain requires an RFC and schema bump.

type.$comment: Role of the source — what kind of thing produced the signal. Orthogonal to `device_class` (physical form factor), `signals` (what is measured), and `transport` (how the bytes reach the producer).

source_tier.$comment: Architectural fidelity of this source. Carried over from HSI 1.2 unchanged. Orthogonal to `quality` (transient) and `signals` (channel availability).

device_class.$comment: Physical form factor. Only meaningful when `type` is a hardware-bearing role (typically `sensor`). Use `other` for unusual form factors; open an RFC before adding new canonical values.

signals.$comment: Physical or logical signals this source produces. Free-form lowercase tokens; suggested canonical names: `hrv`, `rr`, `ecg`, `ppg`, `spo2`, `resp`, `accel`, `gyro`, `mag`, `temp`, `eda`, `gsr`, `eeg`, `emg`, `touch`, `audio`. Consumers SHOULD tolerate unknown entries. Channel availability (e.g. `ppg` vs `touch`) is conveyed here; no separate fidelity tier exists in 1.3.

transport.$comment: How data reaches the producer. `inproc` = same-process APIs. `network` = generic IP when no more specific transport applies.

vendor.$comment: Free-form vendor/manufacturer tag (e.g. `polar`, `whoop`, `garmin`, `apple`). PRIVACY: highest-entropy field in `source`; producers SHOULD omit `vendor` in privacy-sensitive contexts where payloads may be joined across subjects (RFC-HSI-0008 §7).

sources.$comment: Map keys are the authoritative source IDs. evidence_source_ids on axis_reading and embeddings SHOULD reference these keys.

baseline_status.$comment: Payload-level summary, informative only. Consumers MUST gate on per-reading `basis`, not on this field. Scheduled for deprecation in 1.5 (RFC-HSI-0012 §13 Q6).

value.$comment: Coarse categorical token or boolean. The token pattern blocks free text; coordinates, place names, app or site names, window titles, URLs, meeting titles and participants MUST NOT appear (RFC-HSI-0012 §7.3).

source.$comment: How the producer knows the value. When a stated and an inferred value exist for the same field and window, the producer MUST emit the stated one.

confidence.$comment: Required when source == inferred (HSI-1.4-CONTEXT-CONFIDENCE-MISSING); SHOULD be omitted otherwise.

focus_window.$comment: True when the window falls inside a focus block the person set.

place_type.$comment: Environment. A coarse category only; never a place name, address or coordinate.

context_frame.$comment: RFC-HSI-0012 §7.2 and Appendix A. The ten canonical fields have closed vocabularies (§13 Q4); five are environment fields. Extensions use non-canonical field names, follow the same context_field shape, and consumers MUST tolerate them.

items.$comment: entries SHOULD reference keys in meta.provenance.sources. Channel-fidelity is read off each cited source's quality/signals/degraded.

embedding.$comment: Embeddings do not carry per-channel confidence breakdown in 1.3; embedding-level fusion attribution is out of scope.

canonicalization.$comment: Canonicalization method applied to the payload (with `integrity` removed) before hashing. Reserved values per RFC-HSI-0009 §3.1.

content_hash.$comment: Hash of the canonicalized payload with `integrity` removed. Lowercase hex prefixed by `sha256:`. RFC-HSI-0009 §4. IMPORTANT for producers: hashing is NOT self-referential — strip the `integrity` field from the payload object BEFORE canonicalizing and hashing, then attach the resulting hash back into a fresh `integrity` block. Consumers verify by performing the same strip-canonicalize-hash and comparing byte-for-byte.

key_id.$comment: URI or DID identifying the signing key. Resolution is out-of-band per RFC-HSI-0009 §5.

value.$comment: Prefixed signature bytes (e.g. `base64url:...`) over the UTF-8 bytes of `content_hash`. RFC-HSI-0009 §5.

integrity.$comment: Optional payload integrity block per RFC-HSI-0009. Presence does not imply verification — HSI-VALIDATE-BASIC and -STRICT do NOT recompute the hash by default; HSI-VALIDATE-INTEGRITY (RFC-HSI-0009 §7) is the tier that does.
